minutes.headline: Select Board backed a Bright Farms tax-increment deal, shortened to eight years, and licensed Lanni Orchards' wine and beer store.
minutes.summary: The board held a public hearing and granted a wine and malt package store license to Lanni Orchards, and jointly appointed a new Parks Commission member. It discussed a right of first refusal at 250 Howard Street (a tri-party agreement to be drafted by town counsel), heard Bright Farms' tax increment financing proposal, and took a straw poll on Halloween trick-or-treating. It also approved a bond anticipation note renewal, minutes, and the election warrant, and went into executive session.

public_comment.topic: Criticized the town's fast permitting for a company's project compared with residents' experience, and the board's earlier help to school transportation companies.
Asked for a pro forma and side-by-side comparison for the Bright Farms TIF, and raised how equipment would be taxed; also suggested contacting an attorney about the West Street land.

what_happened.line: The Select Board directed that a Bright Farms tax increment financing deal proceed on an eight-year term, kept revenue neutral if possible, with a ten-year version as an alternative.
The board decided the right of first refusal at 250 Howard Street is not waived until a tri-party agreement, drafted by town counsel and the town manager, is in place.
The board granted a wine and malt package store license to Lanni Orchards, 5-0 by roll call.
The board told the town manager to proceed with selling a small town-owned piece at 671 West Street and to notify only the two abutters.
The board approved a bond anticipation note renewal and signed the November 3, 2020 election warrant, both by roll call.

why_it_matters: A tax increment financing deal discounts a company's property taxes for a set number of years, so its term and revenue-neutral condition decide how much new tax revenue the town gives up or collects.

The 250 Howard Street agreement and the 671 West Street sale both affect whether town-held land is protected as open space or passes into private hands, and the Howard Street question may come to residents as a warrant article.
watch_next: The special town meeting warrant article review, which goes first on next week's Select Board agenda.
The tri-party agreement on 250 Howard Street, which town counsel is to draft.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the core votes and most figures (the Lanni license, the Embers 4-1, the warrants, the BAN and the free cash). The main differences are the Sullivan vote count (8-0 in the official minutes, on a five-member board), the BAN renewal vote that the official minutes do not record, and the 671 West Street and 250 Howard Street decisions, which the two records describe differently.
